findings.evidence: 1. Plan: before any edit or delegation, record per requirement its owner, dependency order and acceptance check.
findings.fix: Shorten step 1 to its non-obvious checkpoint (one owner per requirement, no two parallel workers share a file, each requirement has an acceptance check). Drop the general planning wording, which the model and the harness's todo and plan features already cover.

findings.evidence: delegate only when its domain rules or tools add something you lack, since each delegation costs context and needs its own verification
findings.fix: Add a short 'before running workers in parallel, ask:' heuristic. Parallelize only when the file sets are disjoint and each worker has its own acceptance check. Otherwise run workers one after another. This adds a thinking frame for the main serial-or-parallel choice.

findings.evidence: Delegated specialists start without your conversation context: pass file paths and acceptance checks explicitly.
findings.fix: Replace this widely known point with an environment-specific gotcha learned in practice, for example that a specialist run with isolation: worktree commits on a different branch, so its diff must be merged or cherry-picked before the gates run in your worktree.

findings.evidence: 2. Baseline and reproduce: list tests already failing in this worktree under Validation as pre-existing
findings.fix: Move gate discovery ahead of the baseline. Find the gate commands (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, the Makefile, else the toolchain's standard test runner) in step 2 and run them there to record pre-existing failures. Step 5 only finds the gates, so the step 2 baseline cannot be taken as written. Also say whether 'else stop and report it' stops only that requirement or the whole task.
